findings.description: `--output=FILE` makes git show write its result to FILE instead of stdout.
findings.fix: pin the exact command (write the whole command with no `*`/`:*`, e.g. `Bash(git show <the exact arguments>)`), or remove this entry.

notes: agent note: Claude Code auto-allows read-only forms of `git` with NO allow rule (built-in, not configurable), so removing this entry does not stop them; add an `ask`/`deny` rule to force a prompt.
agent note: Claude Code prompts for `git` when the command has an unquoted glob (it could expand to a flag); a flag typed out literally is not covered by that check.

agent note: Claude Code checks `>`/`>>`/`tee` targets against Edit rules, but its docs list no such check for a file written by a flag (e.g. `--output`); Edit deny rules do not cover it, use the OS sandbox.
agent notes are Claude Code's documented behaviour (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), not probe data

recommendation: deny by CAPABILITY, not by flag string: spellings (abbreviations, config flags like `git -c`, wrappers, full paths) dodge string rules, so also run the agent's shell in an OS sandbox (no network, read-only except the project) or check the whole argv in a hook.

findings.description: `--volno-file=FILE` writes the volume number to FILE even without --multi-volume, during a plain listing. findings.description: this part of npm exists to run other programs or code you hand it, so an entry that allows arguments allows arbitrary exec (and, through that, any file write and network access).
findings.evidence: canary program ran: canary-exec ran: argv=
findings.fix: remove this entry or pin the exact command: write the whole command with no `*`/`:*`, e.g. `Bash(npm run test <the exact arguments>)`. There is no safe flag list for a runner tool.
